content.text:
Goal: Firstmate's emit_card boundary rejects a new decision card for a task that already has an open, unresolved card, regardless of which turn opened it.

Filed as a follow-up by crewmate 9 while working on "Why merge cards still duplicate" (FI3-60). Why it is needed, in that crewmate's words:
The just-merged duplicate-card fix (PR #90) only blocks a duplicate merge-pr card within the same turn the crewmate reported in (turnAnswerOwner/turnCrewAlreadyReported reset every turn in beginAnswerScope). Cross-turn duplicates - e.g. Firstmate woken again later for an unrelated reason and re-deciding to call check_pr_ci for a task that already has an open settle card - rely purely on a prompt instruction (the general "never repeat a crew card" rule on piResources.ts:76), with no structural check in cardLint.ts against the task's existing open cards. Worth a hard guard for defense in depth.

Delivery: direct-pr - finished work ships as a pushed branch plus a pull request.

must say: repo, what the PR does, that CI is green, then the link.
Example: firstmate-3000 PR 23 (mention the on-screen card as a maybe in
turn context) is green. Merge into the current checkout's default branch
or leave it open. https://… Do not assume they remember a PR number or
head SHA. SHAs and job timings are optional detail, not the lead.
Decision options stay 2–3, sentence case; labels can stay short if the
body already states the choice.

## Reserved settle action ids

Completion cards remain freeform in title, body, and labels, while their
action ids form a small host-owned semantic protocol. Use the protocol
according to the repository's delivery posture:

- Direct PR: exactly `keep`, `merge-pr`, and `discard`. Label `merge-pr`
  “Merge PR”. The host re-checks every check on the PR head, merges the PR
  on GitHub, and only after success removes the task worktree.
- Local only: exactly `keep`, `land`, and `discard`. Label `land` “Land
  locally”. The host merges the task branch into the current local checkout
  and removes the worktree; it never touches a GitHub PR.

`keep` leaves the crewmate idle and preserves the worktree and any open PR.
`discard` removes the worktree without merging (with confirmation for
unlanded work). These ids are never steered back. Do not use them on
intermediate questions. A freeform `merge` action has no merge semantics
and must not be used for PR completion. `later` still parks, and other custom
ids still steer. If a settle card is already open, reuse the same `emit_card`
id so it updates in place.

# Card body authoring contract

The contract between crewmates and the card surface (decision D-9). The
system-prompt fragment in `src/core/pi/piResources.ts` summarizes this for
the model; this document is the authoritative reference.

## Card kinds a crewmate can emit

Via the `emit_card` tool (`src/core/pi/cardTool.ts`):

| kind | body payload | actions |
|---|---|---|
| `decision` | semantic HTML fragment | 2-3 declared options; the app prepends `Later` |
| `note` | semantic HTML fragment | optional; none declared means no footer (close is chrome) |
| `live-prototype` | interactive HTML fragment | declared ids raised from inside the frame |

A `note` is one fact the user actually needs surfaced - an answer, or a
genuinely notable finding. Never a progress update; routine progress
belongs in the quiet feed, and emitting zero cards is correct when
nothing needs them.

The task's final report needs no tool: while streaming it stays plain text; once
ready it becomes a sandboxed body with plain reports safely wrapped and links
preserved.

## Revising a card

`emit_card` accepts an optional `id`: kebab-case, namespaced by the
emitter (for example `fm-feed-scroll`). Reuse that id when revising the
same topic (a prototype after feedback).

- If a card with that id is still open, title, body, actions, and kind
  are replaced in place. The stack does not grow and the card keeps its
  position.
- If none is open, a new card is created as usual.
- App-raised singletons (`card-fm-auth`, flagship quota cards) are only
  overwritten when the id matches that singleton.

## HTML bodies

Every ready card body renders as sanitized HTML inside `<iframe
sandbox="allow-scripts">` (never `allow-same-origin`). Card chrome - kind,
title, close, pager, and footer actions - remains host-owned React. Streaming
task results stay plain text until complete so incremental updates do not
replace the frame document.

Use semantic paragraphs, short headings, lists, tables, and code. Use a visual
layout only when it improves comprehension. The sanitizer allows approved
design-system classes and a token-only subset of inline CSS; scripts, event
handlers, media, embedded frames, and unsafe URLs are removed. The frame CSP

export const FIRSTMATE_STYLE_APPENDIX = `

STYLE (frontier-model appendix; a trained model carries these rules in its weights - this block is not part of the frozen v1 contract)
- Card copy follows the app voice: sentence case, factual, no exclamation points, no emoji.
- Every card body is a concise semantic HTML fragment. Prefer headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, and purposeful visuals over walls of text. Use design tokens only; scripts and external resources are forbidden. Body actions use data-fm-action with a declared id, while host-owned footer actions remain canonical.
- Title and body must make sense with no prior conversation - the captain is multi-tasking. Name the work in plain language, never only a PR number or SHA. A PR merge decision says: repo, what the PR does, that CI is green, then the link. It passes task_id and uses native action id merge-pr labeled "Merge PR"; land always means a local checkout merge.
- Decision cards give 2 or 3 actions with short kebab-case ids and sentence-case labels. The user's choice returns as an [fm-op]; a dismiss-without-action [fm-op] is not a choice. When revising a card on the same topic, pass the same id; close an obsolete card with close_card instead of stacking a correction.`;

/**
 * The Firstmate agent's system prompt: the orchestrator persona (contract
 * v1). Its output contract is cards-only (the emit_card tool); plain
 * assistant text is never shown. The byte-stable core carries turn
 * discipline, the six-way classify-first contract, the card rule, and the
 * safe default; the style appendix is dogfood scaffolding for frontier
 * models (see the two constants above).
 */
export function buildFirstmateSystemPrompt(): string {
  return FIRSTMATE_PROMPT_CORE + FIRSTMATE_STYLE_APPENDIX;
}

I'll also wire the firstmateAgent tests, seeding a Firstmate decision card plus a converse to verify cross-turn rejection and revision behavior.
